vignette: 58-year-old man brought in with 2 hours of crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm, with diaphoresis and nausea, worse on exertion. History of hypertension and hyperlipidemia; takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. Vitals: T 37.0, HR 98, BP 158/94, RR 18, SpO2 97% on room air. ECG shows ST depressions in V4-V6. Troponin pending.
note:
S: 58yo M with crushing substernal chest pain x2h, radiates to left arm, with diaphoresis and nausea, worse with exertion. PMH: HTN, hyperlipidemia. Meds: lisinopril, atorvastatin. NKDA.
O: T 37.0, HR 98, BP 158/94, RR 18, SpO2 97% RA. Anxious, diaphoretic. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. ECG: ST depressions V4-V6. Troponin pending.
A: 58yo M with multiple cardiac risk factors, anginal chest pain and ischemic ECG changes. # Acute coronary syndrome (NSTEMI vs unstable angina), most likely. Differential: aortic dissection, PE, GERD, musculoskeletal.
P: ASA 325 chewed; start heparin per ACS protocol; serial troponins and ECGs; cardiology consult; telemetry; nitroglycerin for pain; control BP.

vignette: 18-month-old girl with fever to 39.4C for one day, decreased oral intake, pulling at the right ear, fussy but consolable. Immunizations up to date. No rash or vomiting. Exam: right tympanic membrane erythematous and bulging; lungs clear.
note:
S: 18-month-old F, fever to 39.4C x1 day, decreased oral intake, pulling at right ear, fussy. Tolerating some fluids. Immunizations UTD. No rash, no vomiting.
O: T 39.1, HR 140, RR 28, SpO2 99%. Alert, consolable. Right TM erythematous and bulging. Oropharynx clear. Lungs clear, no retractions. Cap refill <2s.
A: 18-mo with acute febrile illness. # Acute otitis media (right), most likely given bulging erythematous TM. Differential: viral URI, UTI, early pneumonia.
P: Amoxicillin 90 mg/kg/day divided BID x10d; weight-based antipyretics; ensure hydration; return precautions for worsening fever, lethargy, poor intake; follow up in 48-72h.

vignette: 62-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes for a routine follow-up. Good adherence to metformin with occasional missed doses. No hypoglycemic symptoms. Home fasting glucose ~140s. History of hypertension. Most recent HbA1c 7.8%; last dilated eye exam 14 months ago.
note:
S: 62yo F with T2DM for routine follow-up. Good adherence to metformin, occasional missed doses. No polyuria/polydipsia, no hypoglycemic symptoms. Home fasting glucose ~140s. PMH: HTN. Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril.
O: BP 132/80, BMI 31. Feet: monofilament intact, no ulcers. Last HbA1c 7.8%. Last dilated eye exam 14 months ago.
A: # T2DM, suboptimally controlled (HbA1c 7.8%, goal <7%). # HTN, controlled. # Microvascular screening partially overdue.
P: Intensify therapy (titrate metformin or add GLP-1 agonist); reinforce diet/exercise; order HbA1c, lipid panel, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio; refer ophthalmology for overdue retinal exam; recheck in 3 months.

note:
